title: SendGrid
content: ## Overview SendGrid is a cloud-based email delivery platform that enables your Emergent app to send transactional and marketing emails reliably. Common use cases include password resets, order confirmations, notifications, and automated email campaigns. This guide shows you how to integrate SendGrid with your Emergent app using environment variables and the SendGrid API. SendGrid offers a free tier with 100 emails per day, which is sufficient for testing and small applications. Production apps typically require a paid plan. ## Prerequisites Before you begin, you'll need: - A SendGrid account ([sign up](https://signup.sendgrid.com/)) - An active Emergent project - Basic familiarity with environment variables ## Setting up SendGrid 1. Log in to your [SendGrid dashboard](https://app.sendgrid.com/) 2. Navigate to **Settings** → **API Keys** 3. Click **Create API Key** 4. Choose **Restricted Access** and enable **Mail Send** permissions (recommended for security) 5. Name your key (e.g., `emergent-production`) 6. Copy the generated API key immediately — it won't be shown again SendGrid requires you to verify the email address or domain you'll send from: 1. Go to **Settings** → **Sender Authentication** 2. For testing: verify a **Single Sender** email address 3. For production: set up **Domain Authentication** to improve deliverability Check your inbox for the verification email and follow the link. In the Emergent chat, add your SendGrid API key as an environment variable: > Add environment variable `SENDGRID_API_KEY` with value `SG.xxxxx...` Mark this variable as **secret** to prevent it from appearing in logs or client-side code. Store your verified sender email as an environment variable for easy reuse: > Add environment variable `SENDGRID_FROM_EMAIL` with value `noreply@yourdomain.com` Optionally add `SENDGRID_FROM_NAME` for a friendly sender name. ## Sending emails from your app Once configured, you can send emails using the SendGrid Node.js SDK or REST API. Here's how to implement common email scenarios: ### Transactional emails ```javascript Node.js (SDK) const sgMail = require('@sendgrid/mail'); sgMail.setApiKey(process.env.SENDGRID_API_KEY); const msg = { to: 'user@example.com', from: process.env.SENDGRID_FROM_EMAIL, subject: 'Your order confirmation', text: 'Thank you for your order #12345', html: 'Thank you for your order #12345', }; await sgMail.send(msg); ``` ```python Python import os from sendgrid import SendGridAPIClient from sendgrid.helpers.mail import Mail message = Mail( from_email=os.environ.get('SENDGRID_FROM_EMAIL'), to_emails='user@example.com', subject='Your order confirmation', html_content='Thank you for your order #12345' ) sg = SendGridAPIClient(os.environ.get('SENDGRID_API_KEY')) response = sg.send(message) ``` ### Using templates SendGrid's Dynamic Templates let you design emails visually and populate them with data: ```javascript const msg = { to: 'user@example.com', from: process.env.SENDGRID_FROM_EMAIL, templateId: 'd-abc123def456', dynamicTemplateData: { userName: 'Alice', orderNumber: '12345', orderTotal: '$99.00', }, }; await sgMail.send(msg); ``` Create templates in the SendGrid dashboard under **Email API** → **Dynamic Templates**. Copy the template ID (starts with `d-`) and pass it in your code. ## Testing email delivery ### Test mode During development, consider these strategies to avoid sending real emails: SendGrid's sandbox mode validates requests without sending actual emails: ```javascript const msg = { // ... your message mailSettings: { sandboxMode: { enable: true, }, }, }; ``` Send all development emails to a test address: ```javascript const to = process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production' ? userEmail : 'test@yourdomain.com'; ``` ### Monitoring delivery Track email activity in the SendGrid dashboard: 1. Go to **Activity** to see recent sends, bounces, and opens 2. Check **Suppressions** for bounced or unsubscribed addresses 3. Review **Statistics** for delivery rates and engagement metrics High bounce rates can damage your sender reputation. Regularly clean your email list and honor unsubscribe requests. ## Common patterns in Emergent apps ### Password reset flow ```javascript // Generate reset token const resetToken = generateSecureToken(); const resetUrl = `${process.env.APP_URL}/reset-password?token=${resetToken}`; await sgMail.send({ to: user.email, from: process.env.SENDGRID_FROM_EMAIL, subject: 'Password reset requested', html: `Click here to reset your password: ${resetUrl}`, }); ``` ### Scheduled notifications Use SendGrid's `sendAt` parameter to schedule emails for a future time (up to 72 hours): ```javascript const sendTime = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + 3600; // 1 hour from now const msg = { to: 'user@example.com', from: process.env.SENDGRID_FROM_EMAIL, subject: 'Reminder: Your appointment is in 1 hour', text: 'See you soon!', sendAt: sendTime, }; ``` ### Batch sending Send the same email to multiple recipients efficiently: ```javascript const msg = { to: ['user1@example.com', 'user2@example.com', 'user3@example.com'], from: process.env.SENDGRID_FROM_EMAIL, subject: 'Team announcement', text: 'Check out our new feature!', }; ``` For large batches (1000+ recipients), consider using SendGrid's batch ID feature to cancel or pause sends if needed. ## Troubleshooting - Verify your sender identity in the SendGrid dashboard - Check the **Activity** feed for delivery status and errors - Ensure `SENDGRID_API_KEY` is set correctly and has **Mail Send** permissions - Look for emails in spam/junk folders (improve this with domain authentication) Your API key likely lacks the necessary permissions. Create a new key with **Mail Send** enabled under **Restricted Access**. Free accounts are limited to 100 emails per day. Upgrade your SendGrid plan or implement retry logic with exponential backoff for production apps. Include an unsubscribe link in marketing emails to comply with regulations: ```javascript const msg = { // ... your message trackingSettings: { subscriptionTracking: { enable: true, }, }, }; ``` SendGrid automatically adds an unsubscribe footer when enabled. ## Best practices Design emails visually in SendGrid and keep HTML out of your codebase. Templates are easier to update and A/B test. Set up SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records to improve deliverability and avoid the spam folder. Wrap `sgMail.send()` in try-catch blocks and log failures for investigation. Don't block user workflows on email delivery. Regularly check bounced and unsubscribed addresses. Remove them from your database to maintain a healthy sender reputation. ## Next steps - Set up [domain authentication](https://docs.sendgrid.com/ui/account-and-settings/how-to-set-up-domain-authentication) for better deliverability - Explore [Dynamic Templates](https://docs.sendgrid.com/ui/sending-email/how-to-send-an-email-with-dynamic-templates) for professional email designs - Configure [webhooks](https://docs.sendgrid.com/for-developers/tracking-events/getting-started-event-webhook) to receive delivery events in your app - Review SendGrid's [email best practices](https://sendgrid.com/blog/10-tips-to-improve-your-email-deliverability/) guide You're now ready to send reliable, professional emails from your Emergent app using SendGrid.
